A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlashDepth and contain readable text, equations, figures and tables. The main content matches closely; v2 adds supplementary Sections 6–8. All supplied pages support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 report original depth-accuracy, boundary-sharpness and runtime experiments, together with super-resolution and model-size ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original temporal-drift results in Figure 5 and recurrent-module comparisons in Table 5.

M1.justification: The Mamba alignment module, hybrid architecture, cross-attention fusion, losses and two-stage training remain unchanged. Transformer and xLSTM substitutions are evaluated as ablations, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets remain unchanged. The added analyses reuse existing Waymo sequences and the five established evaluation datasets: ETH3D, Sintel, Waymo, Unreal4K and UrbanSyn.

E2.justification: The main baseline set and UNet/DAGF comparisons are retained. Table 5 adds xLSTM and a CUT3R-style recurrent transformer as evaluated alternatives to FlashDepth's Mamba module.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds a temporal-drift protocol measuring scale-factor standard deviations over increasing prefixes of 200-frame Waymo sequences. Section 7 compares temporal modules within FlashDepth-L. Section 8.2 additionally reports a VidDepthAny timing check on 32 square 518-pixel frames. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v1's ablations concern super-resolution alternatives and hybrid versus smaller models. v2 substantially expands the analysis to temporal behavior: Figure 5 examines scale drift as sequences lengthen, and Table 5 tests dependence on the recurrent architecture across five datasets.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 5's standard deviations measure temporal scale variation across frames, rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 remain numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantive findings on temporal stability and module alternatives. Figure 5 shows least drift for DepthCrafter, similar drift for FlashDepth and CUT3R, and rapidly increasing VidDepthAny drift. Table 5 adds transformer/xLSTM results, including Unreal4K accuracies of 0.608/0.593 versus Mamba's retained 0.566. The newly reported 71 FPS VidDepthAny check uses different inputs from its retained 24 FPS benchmark.

T1.justification: The method equations and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Section 8.1 spells out the previously used, cited boundary metric; this is additional explanation rather than a new theoretical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: real-time streaming depth at 2K resolution, sharp boundaries, competitive accuracy and limited additional training data. The supplement adds supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: The supplement attributes similar FlashDepth/CUT3R drift to recurrent state and VidDepthAny's drift to local batch alignment. It interprets Table 5 as evidence that the specific recurrent architecture is not crucial, and explains runtime discrepancies through resolution and overlapping batches. The original residual-flickering limitation remains.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised release with a code/weights release statement and repository link. Sections 8.1–8.2 disclose ten boundary thresholds spanning 5–25%, threshold weighting, float16 inference, GPU preloading and timing boundaries. These clarify existing measurements without establishing that they were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds the xLSTM reference for its new ablation and explicitly positions FlashDepth's novelty in integrating existing components for streaming high-resolution depth. The existing related-work discussion and cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 appends supplementary Sections 6–8 while preserving the main narrative and section order. Other edits are limited to the release statement, an aspect-ratio clarification and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The supplement adds Figure 5's temporal-drift plot and Table 5's recurrent-module comparison. Existing Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–4 retain their content and presentation; the additional reference causes limited bibliography reflow.

improvement.justification: The supplement strengthens v1's indirect assessment of temporal consistency with explicit scale-drift evidence and adds a useful recurrent-module ablation. Boundary-metric and timing disclosures improve reproducibility and interpretation, including clarifying that throughput excludes preprocessing and GPU loading. These are meaningful, focused gains while the main method and benchmark results remain unchanged.
